No named-customer delivery or independent demonstration video was found during this research session, so delivery.status is 'claimed'; price figures circulating on aggregator sites (e.g. $150,000+, €110,803.55) could not be traced to a manufacturer or press source and were omitted rather than included unsourced.

Shipped-bar re-check (2026-09-20), applying this site's actual rule (named customer + image via the customer's own or an independent channel; invoice/serial/unboxing/customs are alternatives, not an added requirement): searched specifically for a named hospital, university, or lab publishing its own photo of a GR-1 unit (parallel to the Durham University / Unitree G1 case). None was found -- coverage of Fourier's healthcare/rehab use cases describes GR-1 as designed for hospital and care-home tasks and cites '2,000+ organizations and hospitals' served as a manufacturer-side aggregate claim, but no specific institution's own channel or independent report names itself as a GR-1 recipient with a photo of its unit. This is a genuine evidence gap, not an over-strict reading of the rule, so GR-1/GR-2 remains claimed, not shipped. No fourier-gr-1.json record exists in this dataset; if one is added later, this same gap applies to it.

locomotion left out (2026-09-21): searched the manufacturer's own product/press page and its main launch coverage (The Robot Report / IEEE Spectrum / named outlet where applicable) for a literal quote naming the propulsion ("bipedal", "legs", "walks", "wheeled base", etc.); none of the pages fetched in this pass contained a checkable sentence naming it specifically for GR-2 -- most pages describe height/DOF/speed without ever stating the locomotion type in words. Left out rather than inferred from photos or category. Revisit with a source that states it directly.
